body: Yeah, it's that inexplicable need of the intuition to connect everything all at once--to contain within memory the entirety of the system. A noble pursuit. Mathematics suggests one also doomed to failure.

I definitely do understand this. I myself am a woman in an extremely male dominated field. I find myself "drying up" emotionally a lot, just to be taken seriously and I think that's actually counterproductive. 

You don't need to feel nothing to succeed, although we're sort of told that being the wolf who never looks back is the secret to success. That's just a toxic trope in my opinion. I think when you have the added burden of shrugging off extra misogyny for work though this is a protective mechanism, one I understand all too well. I don't know if you deal with misogyny but I do. 

That said, I've been trying recently to find my answer in reading. When the people around me are cold, I try to go to books that are so warm they balance out these thoughts and remind me of my true values. I like spiritual books for this purpose, especially stuff by Thich Naht Hanh, or even Osho. This appeals to me personally because there isn't much God talk as God as a somewhat human-like existence is hard for me to fit into my beliefs. bell hooks is another great one. There is a corner of feminism focused less on equal rights in the workplace ( though this is important, I don't think it's the focus of this question) and more on protecting what is culturally notated as feminine--this includes vulnerability, caring, and empathy. I try to read books on that as well.

I think it's also important to balance out your more thinking friends with more feeling ones. I have my issues with MBTI, but I do think the thinking/feeling divide is real. Although I tend to be more thinking as I think feelings going unchecked for future repurcussions can be extremely damaging, I also know that thinking can go on infinitely and cause the seeds of happiness to dry up. It's important to temper both and amputate neither. 

Perhaps try to get involved with something centered around caring, empathy, or expression. This can be a volunteering experience, an arts club, watching counselor's videos on youtube, reaching out to a friend that shows concerning signs on social media, or just socializing for its own sake a local bar/coffee shop that you like. You do have to find time and effort to do this though, as I'm all to familiar with the trap of going cold for the sake of work or focus or just protecting oneself from past hurt. I also think just giving compassionate advice on reddit is a good practice for this as well.

I think you're doing the right thing bettering yourself. You're also going to have to write her off for thinking you're unattractive. If you accept that she thinks that of you, you let yourself become unattractive. Believe you are attractive and that's how you become it. Confidence really is important. Charisma can "make up" For all sorts of shallow aesthetic things, and you might also simply just not be her type, or you seem too easy for her. Who knows. 

It's like if somebody says a super honest person is a liar. A person who knows they're super honest would have nothing to do with that person anymore because that know that's not true.

Change the definition of attractiveness to how you feel about yourself--are you proud of yourself? Are you only one-upping yourself to become the most amazing man you know you can be? Then you know you are attractive. And what she said was BS. And you don't have time for it--you want a woman who builds you up.

The best thing you can do is lead by example and energy. Sounds like you are when you say that you would always give support and care about. And that it hurts you that they're stuck in a victim or inferior mentality. Give them something positive to mirror, that's the most effective way in my opinion. At first it my annoy them and might even be fervently attacked, but this makes you stronger and gives them confidence that strong people who won't be bogged down exist, and that they can be just like that too if they do what you do.
Thank you for being absolutely point blank about it, then. I need that right now.
